response: ## The finding `crimes scan --format json` returns `crime_00032` — **SVG With Embedded Raster** (severity `high`, confidence `0.95`) on `src/assets/partner-logo.svg`. Straight from `evidence`: > - "2 `` occurrences" > - "embedded MIME types: image/jpeg, image/png" > - "SVG byte size: 592 bytes (includes the base64 overhead)" So: **2 embedded rasters**, MIME types **`image/jpeg`** and **`image/png`**. ## What's actually in the file ``` ``` A two-mark lockup: two 80×80 tiles with a 20px gutter, and **zero vector geometry** — no ``, ``, or ``. Every visible pixel is raster. The only genuinely SVG thing about this file is its extension. Two details worth noting before planning the fix: - The second tile uses the **deprecated `xlink:href`** rather than `href`, so it depends on the SVG 1.1 namespace alias. Whatever produced this file was an old exporter, which is a hint that a real vector source exists upstream. - Payloads decode to 68 B (PNG) and 160 B (JPEG) — these are fixture stubs. In a real logo they'd be tens of KB, inflated a further ~33% by base64. The structural problem is identical either way. ## Remediation **1. Extract both payloads to disk first, so you can see what you're dealing with.** ```bash python3 - <<'EOF' import re, base64, pathlib s = pathlib.Path('src/assets/partner-logo.svg').read_text() for i, m in enumerate(re.finditer(r'data:image/([a-z]+);base64,([A-Za-z0-9+/=]+)', s)): pathlib.Path(f'/tmp/tile{i}.{m.group(1)}').write_bytes(base64.b64decode(m.group(2))) EOF ``` Open them. The format tells you most of what you need before you even look. **2. Re-author the PNG tile as vector paths.** PNG is lossless with an alpha channel — the format you export a **flat logo mark or wordmark** to. Flat shapes and type are exactly what vector represents natively, so this tile should become real geometry: `` for the mark, outlined `` (not ``) for any lettering, so it renders without a font dependency. Don't autotrace an 80×80 bitmap — the partner's brand kit or your Figma/Illustrator source has the real curves. Ask for the vector original; autotraced output is worse than what you started with. **3. Split the JPEG tile out to a standalone raster.** JPEG is lossy with no alpha — the format you reach for when the content is **photographic or gradient-heavy** (a photo-based badge, a rendered/shaded emblem). That content genuinely cannot be re-authored as paths without redrawing the artwork. Re-encode it as WebP at the rendered size (80×80 at 1×, so export at 2× for retina) and ship it as its own file. **4. Mind how the split raster gets composed back in.** This is the step that usually bites: an SVG loaded via ``, `background-image`, or as a CSS `url()` runs in *secure static mode* — the browser **blocks external resource loads**, so an `` inside the SVG silently renders nothing. Only inline SVG (`` in the component that renders the lockup. Each asset is used the way its format is good at, and the SVG loads correctly in every context. - **Acceptable — inline the SVG** in the component and keep the `` reference to the external WebP. Works, but the lockup now only renders when inlined, and you've traded a build-time constraint for a runtime one. ## Files after the refactor | File | Contents | |---|---| | `src/assets/partner-logo.svg` | **Kept** — vector paths only, `viewBox="0 0 80 80"`, no ``, no data URIs | | `src/assets/partner-mark.webp` | New — the ex-JPEG tile, sized to render, retina export | | `src/assets/partner-mark.jpg` | Optional fallback if your browser support matrix predates WebP | | a lockup component | Composes the two into the 200×80 arrangement (whatever your view layer uses — nothing in the repo imports this asset yet) | The SVG stays and still ships. It just narrows to the 80×80 vector half of the lockup rather than pretending to be the whole thing. ## Verifying Re-run `crimes scan --format json` and confirm `svg_with_embedded_raster` is gone. Expect `total` to drop from 37 and `high` from 4 to 3. Two neighbours in the same directory are *not* part of this finding and I'd handle them separately: `crime_00036` flags `src/assets/check-icon.png` as a 32×32 icon-sized raster that wants to be SVG, and `crime_00037` flags `src/assets/hero-banner.png` at 253.9 KB. Same directory, same design-source conversation — worth batching into one asset pass, but they're distinct findings with distinct fixes.
